definition: the ten-year record of travel putting me past capacity, and the first one that did not

settled:
Every trip in the past ten years was way over the edge of my capacity, so much so that I was consistently physically ill by the end of every trip, just from disruption to my habits and from stress.

The chain ran the same way each time. Travel breaks the habit structure, the disruption and the stress together overload me, and the overload comes out as physical illness by the end of the trip.

Travel is scary. I am healthier now than I have been in ten years, and overwhelm is still my base case.

The sixteen days in Europe were the first in that record to land merely at the edge rather than far past it. I put that down to being the healthiest I have been in a decade, so the same disruption no longer overloads me.

The expectation going in was still overwhelm. The gain showed in how close to the edge the trip landed rather than in what I expected of it.

title: What Every Trip Has Cost Me
